subject: technology
topic: The 'infinite scroll' creates a neurological state of perpetual craving
angle: Infinite scrolling uses intentional variable-ratio reinforcement design to create compulsion loops that replace deep human connection with fragmented interactions.
title: the engineering of the scroll

hooks.text: you think you are browsing, but you are being trapped.
you are participating in a compulsion loop.
a thumb moving over glass in a dark room.
infinite scrolling is an engineered wrong attractor.

reveal.headline: infinite scrolling is an engineered wrong attractor.
reveal.body: Social media addiction is formalized as entrapment in a design built through intentional variable-ratio reinforcement.

explain.headline: the design removes natural stopping points.
explain.body: You are immersed in algorithmic loops. These loops are difficult to break because there are no natural stopping points in the feed.

matters.headline: fragmented interactions replace deep connection.
matters.body: That may be why your social interactions feel ephemeral. The design replaces deep interpersonal relations with fragmented interactions.

example.headline: the late night scroll.
example.body: you sit on the edge of your bed at 11 p.m. your thumb moves rhythmically over the glass while the room stays dark.

stat.label: the design used to create compulsion loops

claims.text: Social media addiction is formalized as entrapment in an engineered wrong attractor built through intentional variable-ratio reinforcement design.
claims.quote: We apply the Displacement Framework to social media addiction, formalizing it as entrapment in an engineered wrong attractor built through intentional variable-ratio reinforcement design.

claims.text: The design of compulsion loops by attention engineers is ethically equivalent to designing addictive products like tobacco.
claims.quote: The intentional design of compulsion loops by attention engineers is analyzed as ethically equivalent to designing addictive products, with tobacco regulation as historical precedent.

claims.text: Infinite scrolling replaces deep interpersonal relations with fragmented, ephemeral interactions.
claims.quote: It replaces deep, sustained interpersonal relations with fragmented, ephemeral interactions, mediated by algorithmic infrastructures optimized for retention rather than human connection.

claims.text: Digital addiction is an overarching concept that is closely related to scrolling syndrome.
claims.quote: This was done as digital addiction is an overarching concept in relation to scrolling syndrome and closely related to the same.

claims.text: Scrolling syndrome shares common criteria with other clinical disorders.
claims.quote: Even for other clinical disorders, common criteria shared with scrolling syndrome have been listed as clinical markers

claims.text: Infinite scrolling immerses users in algorithmic loops that are difficult to break because there are no natural stopping points.
claims.quote: By continuously loading content without natural stopping points (e. g. the end of the page), infinite scrolling immerses users in algorithmic loops that are difficult to break.

verdict: The sources indicate that infinite scrolling is a deliberate design choice that creates difficult-to-break loops and shares clinical markers with other addictions.
caveat: One source is a preprint that has not yet been peer-reviewed.
caption:
Infinite scrolling is a deliberate design choice meant to create compulsion loops. 

Research indicates these loops are engineered using variable-ratio reinforcement and lack natural stopping points. One source is a preprint that has not been peer-reviewed.
